# Test differences in alpha diversity trajectories over time by abx use group
## Read and format data

```{r read.data.factor, include=FALSE}
long_df = read.csv('data/stool_repeat_clients_long.csv',
                  colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

# Want to make sure that categorical vars are factored properly
long_df$sex <- factor(long_df$sex)
long_df$meds_blood_sugar <- factor(long_df$meds_blood_sugar)
long_df$meds_cholesterol <- factor(long_df$meds_cholesterol)
long_df$abx_recency <- factor(long_df$abx_recency)
long_df$vendor_dashboard <- factor(long_df$vendor_dashboard)

# Let's mean center our age and GFR
# redoing GFR because the slice of the data may be different
long_df$centered_age <- long_df$age - mean(long_df$age)
```

```{r check.abx.ref, include=FALSE}
levels(long_df$abx_recency) # Checking the "none" abx is the reference
```

```{r decompose.bmi}
long_df$bmi_person_mean = ave(long_df$BMI_CALC, # For column BMI
                      long_df$public_client_id, # Group by person
                      FUN = mean) 

# To find person-specific deviation of a particular time point
long_df$bmi_within = (long_df$BMI_CALC -        # For each time point
                      long_df$bmi_person_mean)  # Subtract person-mean


# To compare from person to person 
long_df$bmi_between = scale(long_df$bmi_person_mean, # Subtract grand-mean from person-mean
                            scale=FALSE)             # Do not z-score
```

```{r create.time.window.var}
long_df$time_100 <- long_df$dsb / 100
```

```{r set.up.models}
outcomes = c('observed_features','berger_parker','shannon_index')

time_by_abx = 'time_100*abx_recency'       # Use for interaction models
time_plus_abx = 'time_100 + abx_recency'   # Remove interaction for LRT

covars_no_time = c('centered_age', 'sex', 'meds_blood_sugar', 'meds_cholesterol', 'PC1',
                   'PC2', 'PC3', 'PC4', 'PC5', 'centered_eGFR', 'vendor_dashboard',
                   'bmi_within', 'bmi_between')
```


## Run models with interaction

Going to try running the model with observed features to get a hang of model
specification.

```{r model.obs.test}
mod_obs <- lmer(observed_features ~ time_100*abx_recency + sex + centered_age + 
                  meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + centered_eGFR + 
                  PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + vendor_dashboard + bmi_within + 
                  bmi_between + (1 | public_client_id),
             data=long_df)

#summary(mod_obs)
```

```{r check.icc}
icc(mod_obs)
```
Looks like around 70% of the variation is between people, so using the random intercept
is helpful!

### Vectorized below

```{r run.int.models}
models_interaction <- setNames(lapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  fixed_terms <- c(time_by_abx, covars_no_time)
  formula <- reformulate(fixed_terms, response = outcome)
  mod <- lmer(update(formula, . ~ . + (1|public_client_id)), # Create model
              data = long_df)
  attr(mod, "outcome") <- outcome # Attach outcome name to the model
  mod                             # Return the model object
  }), 
  outcomes)                   # Names the list index (uses setNames)
  
# formula(models_interaction$observed_features) # Used to see which formula was used
```

## Run models without interaction

```{r run.add.models}
models_additive <- setNames(lapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  fixed_terms <- c(time_plus_abx, covars_no_time)
  formula <- reformulate(fixed_terms, response = outcome)
  mod <- lmer(update(formula, . ~ . + (1|public_client_id)), # Create model
              data = long_df)
  attr(mod, "outcome") <- outcome # Attach outcome name to the model
  mod                             # Return the model object
  }), 
  outcomes)                   # Names the list index (uses setNames)
```

## Perform LRT

```{r lrt.all.alphas}
LRT_pvals <- setNames(sapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  anova(
    models_additive[[outcome]],
    models_interaction[[outcome]]
  )$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
}), outcomes)

LRT_pvals
```

```{r FDR.adjustment}
# Extract just the numbers
pvals_num <- unlist(LRT_pvals)   
qvals <- p.adjust(pvals_num, method = "BH")

results_lmm_alphas <- data.frame(
  name = names(pvals_num),
  p_value = pvals_num,
  q_value = qvals
)

results_lmm_alphas
```

Awesome, looks like all of these meet q<0.1, suggesting that having the interaction
between the time*group variable (i.e., different slopes for the antibiotic users)
was helpful in modeling the data. This may suggest that the recovery trajectory 
was different between the antibiotic use groups. Let's go ahead and look at the data
some more. 

## Interpretation

```{r print.formula}
formula(models_interaction$observed_features)
```
```{r get.estimates}
models_interaction$observed_features
```
Looks like the average person in the reference/none group showed a slight
decrease in the number of observed features over time. In particular, it's a decrease
of -0.29 features over a period of 100 days. However, the individuals in the 
antibiotic groups have a different slope.

- **Three month group:**  -0.2916 + 1.1888  = 0.8972
- **Twelve month group:** -0.2916 + 0.4788  = 0.1872

In all cases, the magnitude of the change is quite small, but it is interesting
that the change is greatest/most positive for the 3 month group.

```{r}
summary(models_interaction$observed_features)
```

## Assess model assumptions

```{r check.VIF}
check_collinearity(models_interaction$observed_features)
```
```{r plot.resid.function}
plot_residuals <- function(model) {
  df <- data.frame(
    Fitted = fitted(model),
    Residuals = residuals(model, type = "pearson")
  )
  
  outcome_name <- attr(model, "outcome")
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Fitted, y = Residuals)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Residuals vs Fitted:", outcome_name),
      x = "Fitted values",
      y = "Pearson residuals"
    ) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size=10, color = "blue"))
}
```


```{r plot.lca.models}
model_list <- models_interaction             # List of LCA models
plots_resids <- lapply(model_list, plot_residuals)  # Individual plots

# Combine plots into a single figure
combined_plot <- plot_grid(plotlist = plots_resids, ncol = 3)

combined_plot # Display
```
# Test dietary behavior as a moderator of abx:time

## Starting with a model using baseline and follow-up dietary questionnaires

Unfortunately, not everyone filled out the dietary questionnaire a second time, 
so I don't really expect to see much, but we can see! For now let's only start 
by testing observed features.

```{r diet.base.follow}
diet_df = read.csv('data/stool_diet_followup.csv',
                  colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

# Want to make sure that categorical vars are factored properly
diet_df$sex <- factor(diet_df$sex)
diet_df$meds_blood_sugar <- factor(diet_df$meds_blood_sugar)
diet_df$meds_cholesterol <- factor(diet_df$meds_cholesterol)
diet_df$abx_recency <- factor(diet_df$abx_recency)
diet_df$vendor_dashboard <- factor(diet_df$vendor_dashboard)

# Let's mean center our age and GFR
# redoing GFR because the slice of the data may be different
diet_df$centered_age <- diet_df$age - mean(diet_df$age)

diet_df$time_100 <- diet_df$dsb / 100
```

```{r diet.decomp.bmi}
diet_df$bmi_person_mean = ave(diet_df$BMI_CALC, # For column BMI
                      diet_df$public_client_id, # Group by person
                      FUN = mean) 

# To find person-specific deviation of a particular time point
diet_df$bmi_within = (diet_df$BMI_CALC -        # For each time point
                      diet_df$bmi_person_mean)  # Subtract person-mean


# To compare from person to person 
diet_df$bmi_between = scale(diet_df$bmi_person_mean, # Subtract grand-mean from person-mean
                            scale=FALSE)             # Do not z-score
```

Now we should also make sure to decouple the between and within time variance
for the dietary variables of interest. Also, the diet columns were not filled out
to the same extent, so we will have to make sub-datasets to drop NAs. 

```{r generate.sub.data.numeric}
diet_vars = c('breakfast', 'cruciferous_vegetables_frequency', 'snack',
              'fruits_per_day', 'vegetables_per_day', 'sugary_drinks_per_day',
              'alcohol_drinks_a_day', 'grains_per_day')

exposure = 'abx_recency'

covars = c('centered_age', 'sex', 'bmi_within', 'bmi_between',
           'meds_blood_sugar', 'meds_cholesterol', 
           'PC1', 'PC2', 'PC3', 'PC4', 'PC5', 'centered_eGFR', 
           'vendor', 'vendor_dashboard',  # For diet and stool, respectively
           'time_100')


# Let's vectorize creating all of our sub-datasets
subdat_diet_vars <- lapply(diet_vars, function(diet_var) {
  diet_df[complete.cases(diet_df[, c(exposure, covars, diet_var)]), ]
})

names(subdat_diet_vars) <- diet_vars # Name them
```

```{r decompose.cruciferous}
subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$avg_cru_freq = ave(
  subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency, # For column
  subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$public_client_id, # Group by person
  FUN = mean) 

# To find person-specific deviation of a particular time point
subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$cru_freq_within = (
  # For each time point
  subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency - 
 subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$avg_cru_freq)  # Subtract person-mean


# To compare from person to person 
subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$cru_freq_between = scale(
  # Subtract grand-mean from person-mean
  subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency$avg_cru_freq, 
  scale=FALSE)             # Do not z-score
```


```{r test.obs.cruc}
mod_obs <- lmer(observed_features ~ time_100*abx_recency + 
                  time_100*cru_freq_between*abx_recency +
                  sex + centered_age + 
                  meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + centered_eGFR + 
                  PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + vendor_dashboard + bmi_within + 
                  bmi_between + (1 | public_client_id),
             data=subdat_diet_vars$cruciferous_vegetables_frequency)

summary(mod_obs)
```

## Shift to looking at dietary behaviors at baseline: CONTINUOUS

This question would hopefully address how the dietary behaviors of individuals
at the beginning of the Arivale program affected their recovery trajectory over
time. I will only be testing observed features as an outcome as this seems to be
the most sensitive metric. 

```{r read.data.diet.baseline}
diet_base = read.csv('data/stool_repeat_diet_baseline_only.csv',
                     colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"), 
                     na.strings = c("", "NA"))
```

```{r clean.vars.again}
# Want to make sure that categorical vars are factored properly
diet_base$sex <- factor(diet_base$sex)
diet_base$meds_blood_sugar <- factor(diet_base$meds_blood_sugar)
diet_base$meds_cholesterol <- factor(diet_base$meds_cholesterol)
diet_base$abx_recency <- factor(diet_base$abx_recency)
diet_base$vendor_dashboard <- factor(diet_base$vendor_dashboard) # Microbiome
diet_base$vendor <- factor(diet_base$vendor)                     # Diet Questionnaire
diet_base$alcohol_type <- factor(diet_base$alcohol_type)

# Let's mean center our age and GFR
# redoing GFR because the slice of the data may be different
diet_base$centered_age <- diet_base$age - mean(diet_base$age)

diet_base$time_100 <- diet_base$dsb / 100
```

```{r decompose.bmi.again}
diet_base$bmi_person_mean = ave(diet_base$BMI_CALC, # For column BMI
                      diet_base$public_client_id, # Group by person
                      FUN = mean) 

# To find person-specific deviation of a particular time point
diet_base$bmi_within = (diet_base$BMI_CALC -        # For each time point
                      diet_base$bmi_person_mean)  # Subtract person-mean


# To compare from person to person 
diet_base$bmi_between = scale(diet_base$bmi_person_mean, # Subtract grand-mean from person-mean
                            scale=FALSE)             # Do not z-score
```

```{r check.alc.preference.coding}
levels(diet_base$alcohol_type)
```

```{r}
diet_vars = c('breakfast', 'cruciferous_vegetables_frequency',
              'fruits_per_day', 'vegetables_per_day', 'sugary_drinks_per_day',
              'alcohol_drinks_a_day', 'grains_per_day', 'alcohol_type')

covars_no_time = c('centered_age', 'sex', 'meds_blood_sugar', 'meds_cholesterol',
                   'PC1','PC2', 'PC3', 'PC4', 'PC5', 'centered_eGFR', 'vendor',
                   'vendor_dashboard','bmi_within', 'bmi_between')
```

```{r nas.in.diet.vars}
na_counts_outcomes <- colSums(is.na(diet_base[, diet_vars]))
print(na_counts_outcomes)
```
Awesome; now that we've looked through the data, we can start fitting models.

### Three-way interaction models

Do any of these dietary behaviors affect the recovery from antibiotics over time?

```{r int.models.diet}
models_diet_int <- setNames(
  lapply(diet_vars, function(mod) {    # mod for moderator
    # Build formula
    interaction_term <- paste0("time_100 * abx_recency * ", mod)
    right_hand <- c(interaction_term, covars_no_time)
    formula <- reformulate(right_hand, response = "observed_features")
    # Fit and name model
    model <- lmer(update(
      formula, . ~ . + (1 | public_client_id)), data = diet_base)
    attr(model, "moderator") <- mod
    model                              # Returns model object              
  }),
  diet_vars
)

# formula(models_LCA_interaction$OXLDL) # Used to see which formula was used
```

### Additive model
This specifically removes the three-way interactions while still allowing for 
the two-way interactions.

```{r mod.diet.add}
models_diet_add <- setNames(
  lapply(diet_vars, function(mod) {
    # Build all 2-way terms manually
    right_hand <- c(
      "time_100 * abx_recency",
      paste0("time_100 * ", mod),
      paste0("abx_recency * ", mod),
      covars_no_time
    )
    formula <- reformulate(right_hand, response = "observed_features")
    
    # Fit and name models
    model <- lmer(update(formula, . ~ . + (1 | public_client_id)),
                  data = diet_base)
    attr(model, "moderator") <- mod
    model
  }),
  diet_vars
)
```

### Perform LRT for diet models

```{r lrt.function}
lrt_results_diet <- mapply(function(reduced, full) {
  anova(reduced, full)
}, models_diet_add, models_diet_int, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
```


```{r build.q.df}
pvals_diet <- sapply(lrt_results_diet, function(x) x$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])

# Extract just the numbers
pvals_num_diet <- unlist(pvals_diet)   
qvals_diet <- p.adjust(pvals_num_diet, method = "BH")

results_lmm_diet <- data.frame(
  name = names(pvals_num_diet),
  p_value = pvals_num_diet,
  q_value = qvals_diet
)

results_lmm_diet[order(results_lmm_diet$q_value), ]
```

Take a look sat fruit in more detail.

```{r}
mod_obs <- lmer(observed_features ~ time_100*abx_recency*fruits_per_day + 
                  sex + centered_age + meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol +
                  centered_eGFR + PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + bmi_within + 
                  bmi_between + vendor + vendor_dashboard  + (1 | public_client_id),
             data=diet_base)
summary(mod_obs)
```

```{r em.trends.cont.fruit}
emtrends(models_diet_int$fruits_per_day,
         ~ abx_recency * fruits_per_day,
         var = "time_100")
```

## Alright, time to fit our models!

### Interaction

```{r models.int.binary}
models_diet_int_binary <- setNames(
  lapply(diet_vars, function(mod) {    # mod for moderator
    # Build formula
    interaction_term <- paste0("time_100 * abx_recency * ", mod)
    right_hand <- c(interaction_term, covars_no_time)
    formula <- reformulate(right_hand, response = "observed_features")
    # Fit and name model
    model <- lmer(update(
      formula, . ~ . + (1 | public_client_id)), data = diet_binarized)
    attr(model, "moderator") <- mod
    model                              # Returns model object              
  }),
  diet_vars
)
```

### Fit additive model

```{r model.add.binary}
models_diet_add_binary <- setNames(
  lapply(diet_vars, function(mod) {
    # Build all 2-way terms manually
    right_hand <- c(
      "time_100 * abx_recency",
      paste0("time_100 * ", mod),
      paste0("abx_recency * ", mod),
      covars_no_time
    )
    formula <- reformulate(right_hand, response = "observed_features")
    
    # Fit and name models
    model <- lmer(update(formula, . ~ . + (1 | public_client_id)),
                  data = diet_binarized)
    attr(model, "moderator") <- mod
    model
  }),
  diet_vars
)
```


```{r lrt.diet.binary}
lrt_results_diet_binary <- mapply(function(reduced, full) {
  anova(reduced, full)
}, models_diet_add_binary, models_diet_int_binary, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
```
```{r check.results.binary}
pvals_diet_binary <- sapply(lrt_results_diet_binary, function(x) x$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])

# Extract just the numbers
pvals_num_diet_binary <- unlist(pvals_diet_binary)   
qvals_diet_binary <- p.adjust(pvals_num_diet_binary, method = "BH")

results_lmm_diet_binary <- data.frame(
  name = names(qvals_diet_binary),
  p_value = pvals_num_diet_binary,
  q_value = qvals_diet_binary
)

results_lmm_diet_binary[order(results_lmm_diet_binary$q_value), ]
```
Alright, looks like none of the binarized dietary variables significantly modifies
the trajectory over time for the antibiotic users. This is not entirely surprising
though as the `time_100`*`abx_recency` interaction term was small to begin with (so
we are estimating a small change of an already small change)

```{r}
emtrends(models_diet_int_binary$alcohol_type,
         ~ abx_recency * alcohol_type,
         var = "time_100")
```


```{r}
# eventually we want emmeans
emm_fruit <- emmeans(models_diet_int_binary$fruits_per_day_binary,
               ~ abx_recency * fruits_per_day_binary | time_100,
               at = list(time_100 = seq(0, max(diet_binarized$time_100), length.out = 50)))

emm_fruit_df <- as.data.frame(emm_fruit)
```


```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = diet_binarized,
            aes(x = time_100, y = observed_features, group = public_client_id, color = abx_recency),
            alpha = 0.15) +

  geom_line(data = emm_fruit_df,
            aes(x = time_100, y = emmean, color = abx_recency),
            size = 1.2) +

  facet_wrap(~ fruits_per_day_binary) +
  theme_minimal()
```
